what: Human ratings of the real-model translation pass (real-translation.json → <id>.png). A = unmistakable, B = recognisable, C = generic creature, D = wrong. Rated by looking at the JUDGE pane alone and then with the source. Two rounds: round 1 is the composer as first run; round 2 is after four GENERIC composer fixes (symmetric spans became mirrored pairs, spans honour their side, limbs to a side are not feet, a light whose partner was dropped rejoins what it hung from, survive outranks width, the budget floors at the essentials). No creature was repaired individually between the rounds — the same seventeen plans were recomposed.
goldenTest: The brief's golden image (the uploaded baby dragon) is not in the repository and cannot be run from here. lumo (the product's own dragon Companion, VihuPlanet's Lumo) is the stand-in for both 'the golden test' and 'a smiling dragon'.

verdict: NO — not yet. The plan captures the right semantics (17/17 valid on the first attempt: the gesture kind, the flow order and the relationships are almost always what a person would say), and the composer turns every one of them into the SAME KIND of figure: a spine with diamonds for volume and spikes for attachments. What a species lives in — the outline of a wing, the curl of a tail, the width of an ear, a pot's flat top — is exactly what a spine-plus-attachment vocabulary cannot draw. It fails at ABSTRACTION in the composer, not at understanding in the model.
